quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely so you can see clearly. Move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do if a traffic signal is not working?

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic signal like a four-way stop. You must come to a complete stop and look both ways before entering the intersection, unless a police officer is directing traffic.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Stop.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They have slower reflexes than adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Children on bikes may suddenly ride onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights from oncoming cars also cause glare. Always use your headlights and drive carefully in the dark.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, you should slow down:

options.text: Before entering the curve.
After finishing the curve.
In the middle of the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Going too fast can cause your tires to slip on the road.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Truck blind spots are very large. The truck driver cannot see your car behind or beside the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: A round sign means railroad tracks are ahead. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Pull to the right side and come to a complete stop.
Keep driving but try to stay out of the way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing red or blue lights, pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check behind and to the side of your vehicle. Make sure no vehicles are in your way before you enter the lane.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?

options.text: It turns sharply right, then left.
It curves right, then left.
It curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: It curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will curve to the right, then to the left.

questions.question: What can speed up how fast alcohol leaves your body?

options.text: Nothing. Only time will remove all alcohol from your body.
Taking a cold shower.
Eating a large meal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing. Only time will remove all alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes about 90 percent of alcohol from your body. It removes alcohol at a rate of about one drink per hour. Nothing can speed this up.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: It makes you worry about the cost of the call.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind away from driving.
Other drivers pay attention to you using it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind away from driving.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it uses your eyes, hands, and mind. Even skilled drivers have a higher risk of crashing when using a cell phone.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap in traffic that is large enough for you to safely merge. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you drive better.
Make you feel better.
Reduce your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You cannot turn left here.
You can turn left only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn left here.
questions.explanation: Signs with a red circle and line through a symbol mean that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use low beam lights in fog. If the fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull over and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many skills needed for safe driving, such as reaction time, coordination, alertness, and focus.

questions.question: What can happen when you take prescription drugs and drink alcohol together?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
You will be more alert.
You may become unsafe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may become unsafe to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can reduce your ability to drive safely. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and a stop arm, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Continue driving when children have finished exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
questions.explanation: Come to a full stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing. Stay stopped until the arm is raised and the lights turn off.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Just the driver
Only children
All passengers and the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers and the driver
questions.explanation: Wyoming law requires all passengers and the driver to wear a safety belt. The driver is responsible for making sure everyone follows this rule. Children must use proper child-restraint systems.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibration to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to alert tired or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road splits ahead and you must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy, your tires do not grip as well as they do on dry roads. You should reduce your speed.

questions.question: When entering an interstate from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Force your way into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from an entrance ramp, you must let traffic already on the highway go first. Merge into traffic safely when you have space.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Construction or maintenance work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction or maintenance work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. They help guide drivers and pedestrians safely through dangerous zones. Traffic fines may double in these areas.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour or so on long trips to avoid tired driving. When possible, share driving with another person so you can each rest while the other drives.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane with no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked. Even without a crosswalk, give pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: A vehicle coming toward you at night has bright high beams on. You cannot see the road well. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would behind a regular car.
Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back behind a large truck than a regular car. Trucks have larger blind spots, so you need more distance.

questions.question: You see a deep puddle on the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed the same to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if you can.
Put the car in neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: When you turn left at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic that is going straight pass first. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without using your signal.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without using your signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. Do not back up or make U-turns on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: Must you obey instructions from a school crossing guard?

options.text: Yes, at all times.
Only during school hours.
Not if you do not see any children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, at all times.
questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Stay alert and follow their instructions.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can cause other drivers to become frustrated and make unsafe passing moves. It is safest to drive with traffic flow and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian crossing your lane with no crosswalk nearby. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before you go.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass here.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass here.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass another vehicle in that area. Visibility is limited, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: What message appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagon sign (eight-sided) always means "stop." You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Drive slightly faster.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: What should you do when a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street?

options.text: Always yield the right-of-way.
Tell them where to cross.
Only yield if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Mirrors do not show everything behind your car. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead has many curves. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Both directions may pass.
The side with the broken line may pass.
The side with the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side with the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass.

questions.question: What should you do if you meet an aggressive driver?

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not compete with other drivers. Respect and cooperate with all road users.

questions.question: What should you do before driving after taking medicine?

options.text: Ask your doctor if it affects driving.
Have someone follow you home.
Keep your window open and drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor if it affects driving.
questions.explanation: Many medicines, including over-the-counter drugs, can affect your ability to drive. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about how a medicine will affect you before driving.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road, but an oncoming car is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first.
Keep going. The oncoming car must stop for you.
Honk your horn so the pedestrian moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one traffic problem at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian when it is safe.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beams.
Parking lights.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What is an important step before turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to turn safely.
